title: A tuple in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring is regular exactly at the expected dimension drop
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of finite Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] with $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. For every integer $r\ge0$ and every $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in\mathfrak m$, the tuple $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ is an $R$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] if and only if $\dim\bigl(R/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\bigr)=d-r$.

source.place: Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM), the displayed equivalence for $x_1,\ldots,x_c\in\mathfrak m$; its Cohen–Macaulay hypothesis is the depth-dimension equality for the local ring.

proof.text: Assume first that $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ is regular. Apply the Mathlib equality in [lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula] to the list $[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. The finite-dimension hypothesis means that $\operatorname{ringKrullDim}(R)=(d:\operatorname{WithBot}\,\mathbb N_\infty)$, so, writing $a=\operatorname{ringKrullDim}(R/(x_1,\ldots,x_r))$ and identifying the list length with $r$, we have $a+(r:\operatorname{WithBot}\,\mathbb N_\infty)=(d:\operatorname{WithBot}\,\mathbb N_\infty)$. This equality also supplies the finiteness and nonzero checks that are needed before using ordinary natural-number arithmetic: if $a=\bot$ (the zero quotient), then the left side is $\bot$, and if $a=\top$ (infinite dimension), then the left side is $\top$; neither can equal the finite natural on the right. Hence $a=(q:\operatorname{WithBot}\,\mathbb N_\infty)$ for a unique $q\in\mathbb N$, so the quotient is nonzero and has finite Krull dimension $q$. Injectivity of the natural embedding into $\operatorname{WithBot}\,\mathbb N_\infty$ now turns the displayed equality into $q+r=d$ in $\mathbb N$. Therefore $r\le d$ and $q=d-r$; if $r>d$, the equation $q+r=d$ is impossible, so this case yields no regular sequence and the implication is vacuous. For $r=0$, the same calculation gives $q=d$ and the quotient is $R$. Thus in every regular case $\dim(R/(x_1,\ldots,x_r))=d-r$.

Conversely, the existing Cohen–Macaulay dimension-drop lemma applies with $c=r$ and $g_i=x_i$: its hypotheses are exactly that $R$ is Noetherian local of finite dimension $d$, depth$(R)\ge d$, each $x_i$ lies in $\mathfrak m$, and the quotient has dimension $d-r$. It concludes that $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ is an $R$-regular sequence.
